issues.description: The problem statement and template expect a no-argument Rideable.messageOnRide() that returns a String (text examples show "Riding on [Animal Type] [name]"). The solution implements Rideable.messageOnRide(int speed) (and Pig/Seal implement the version with an int parameter). This parameter mismatch creates a structural conflict: students following the problem/template will implement/expect messageOnRide() without parameters, while the solution uses a different signature.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the Rideable interface and all implementations consistent with the problem statement and template: change Rideable.messageOnRide(int) to messageOnRide() returning String, and update Pig/Seal implementations accordingly to return "Riding on [Animal Type] [name]". Alternatively, if the speed parameter is intended pedagogically, update the problem statement and template code (including examples in Main and the UML) to specify messageOnRide(int speed) and adjust the textual examples to include the speed.

issues.description: The method signature for messageOnRide differs between the problem statement / template usage and the solution: the problem UML and template Main expect messageOnRide() with no parameters, but the solution's Rideable interface and implementing classes define messageOnRide(int speed). This mismatch breaks the direct mapping students rely on (the template Main calls r.messageOnRide() without an argument) and creates confusion about the required method signature.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the method signature consistent across all artifacts. Either revert the solution to implement messageOnRide() with no parameters in Rideable, Pig, and Seal (and update their implementations accordingly), or update the problem statement and template to require messageOnRide(int speed) and adjust usages (e.g., calls in Main and the UML) to pass the speed parameter. Prefer aligning the solution to the problem/template to avoid student confusion.
